exit_codes.description:
Every process exit status this build can return, with its machine
code, recovery class and provenance. Derived from the error enum
(B3) so the list cannot drift from the code that produces it.

flag_contract.description:
Flag semantics that are contract rather than prose: what each flag
means and which combinations the CLI rejects.

discovery.description: How to discover the schema surface without parsing help text.

ok.description: Outcome of the run, stamped by the writer

code.description: Machine error code, present when ok is false

exit.description: Process exit status, present when ok is false

target_resolved.description: Absolute target the run resolved, or `-` for standard input; several subjects are joined with `,` in invocation order

target_source.description: Where the target came from: named in the invocation line, inherited from the workspace slot, or the standard-input stream

workspace_source.description: Where the workspace root came from: the `--workspace` flag or the process working directory

records_suppressed.description: Records the writer dropped before the terminal event: `--filter` rejections, `--select` projections that emptied the record, dedupe duplicates and `--limit` cuts. It counts records, never files, so it does not compare with `files_matched`: one file can contribute several records

files_budget_dropped.description: Entries the `--limit` budget dropped, in the unit the verb produces: files for walking verbs, records for streaming ones; a floor, because workers may stop before producing the rest

files_planned.description: Files the run would have modified in `--dry-run` or `--preview`; absent from a run that really wrote

truncated.description: The record itself was cut by `--truncate-content` or `--max-output-bytes`, so the fields are shorter than the source

truncated_records.description: Records the writer cut this run, counted once per record

available.description: Whether the tool is usable in this build (A-009).

install_hint.description: Optional rebuild / install hint when `available` is false.

ExitCodeEntry.description: One exit status of the process, derived from an error variant.

code.description: Numeric status the process returns to the shell.

name.description: Machine-readable error code, or the process-level label.

retryable.description: Whether retrying the same operation may succeed.

source.description:
Provenance: `error-variant` (derived from the error enum) or
`process` (status produced by the runtime, not by an error variant).

FlagContractEntry.description: One flag whose semantics are part of the agent contract.

flag.description: Flag name as accepted on the command line.

semantics.description: What the flag means, including the combinations the CLI rejects.

DiscoveryEntry.description:
The schema-discovery door, published so an agent can find it by field.

Without this, discovering that a schema dump exists at all meant reading
`--help` prose and hoping the wording survived a release. The names come from
[`crate::SCHEMA_NAMES`], the same list the dispatcher serves, so the count
here cannot drift from what `--print-schema` actually answers.

flag.description: Global flag that answers both forms.

schema_names.description: Every schema name this build serves, alphabetically ordered.
